title: Review of c30's Complex Hash contests: all four rules replicate on fresh seed 5; zero-sum churns at 0-4 significant kinds per window out of ~146k births, the feature contest sits at the neutral rate (88-222 per window), transitive freezes (top kind 71-89%, size 1.05-1.14)
summary: Copied c30's world.py, run.py and analyze.py unchanged into this directory (run.py writes next to itself) and ran the four rules for 20000 steps on fresh seed 5 (~2020 complexes), then analyze.py with the neutral twin of the same seed setting a* = 470. Late (t >= 2000) significant kinds per 1000-step window: neutral 18-198 (78.9k births per window), zero-sum 0-4 (146k births, 0.00-0.03 per 1000), feature 88-222 (72.8k births, 1.2-3.0 per 1000), transitive 0-3 (2.5k births). Transitive: commonest kind 0.71-0.89 of complexes throughout, mean size 1.05-1.14; zero-sum: commonest kind 1-2%, mean size 13.5-14.4 of the cap 16; feature: size drifts 3.4-9.8. Every figure falls in the range c30 reports for seeds 0-2.

observations.finding: calibrated.json (seed 5, a*=470): zero-sum sig per window 0-4 after t=2000; feature 88-222; neutral 18-198; transitive 0-3; runs/tr_s5.json topshare 0.71-0.89, msize 1.05-1.14; runs/zs_s5.json topshare 0.011-0.019, msize 13.5-14.4

controls_run.finding: runs/neu_s5.json (in-world neutral twin, same seed) sets a* for the other three rules

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at the finding's single parameter set. The last window (t=19000) reads 0 in every rule because kinds born there cannot finish their 1000-step activity count. The labkit run (labkit_feat, t=1500) is only a visual check; labkit finds no components in this particle world, so the cohort measure carries the result.
